  owner: Hubert Dunn, clock keeper
  date: 11 to 23 December 1958

::: handwriting
**11 Dec.** Big brass winding key gone from its hook by the window, so I wound the clock at 6 p.m. with the little spare key, which gives only a half winding: nine hours and seventeen minutes.

**12 Dec.** Clock stood at 3:17 when I came up. Every morning at 7 a.m. I set the hands and give a second half winding with the spare key, so the clock runs to 4:17 p.m. and the four o'clock whistle still blows.

**21 Dec.** I am ashamed to write it, but I slept in the gate hut from half past two until four.

**22 Dec.** Saw something at the louvre with Miss Okafor. Went up. On the dusty top step I saw the print of a smooth town shoe. Miss Okafor and I both wear boots. On a sharp edge of the clock works, beside the speaking tube, hung a torn scrap of dark red silk, like a piece of a tie. Behind the dial I found a heap of twigs, and in it the big winding key, seven robot keys, a thimble, sweet papers, and a gold tie pin shaped like a television aerial. Everything in the nest came from our own works, the keys, the thimble from the packing hall, the sweet papers from our canteen, all except that pin. Who hid them here?

**23 Dec, 7 a.m.** Wound with the big key at 6 p.m. yesterday, and the clock ran all night without a stop.
:::
